## Objective
Determine which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) on the West Coast of the US are best suited to developing marine aquaculture for several species of oysters and *Mytilus galloprovincialis* (Mediterranean mussels). Suitable locations will be determined based on range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species.

## Load packages
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

library(tidyverse)
library(spDataLarge)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(gt)
library(viridisLite)
library(terra)
library(stars)
library(kableExtra)
```

## Prepare data 

```{r}
# Load EEZ data
eez <- st_read("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/wc_regions_clean.shp")

# Load bathymetry data
depth <- rast("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/depth.tif")

# Load SST rasters
sst8 <- rast("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/average_annual_sst_2008.tif")
sst9 <- rast("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/average_annual_sst_2009.tif")
sst10 <- rast("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/average_annual_sst_2010.tif")
sst11 <- rast("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/average_annual_sst_2011.tif")
sst12 <- rast("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-aquaculture/data/average_annual_sst_2012.tif")
```

# Process data
```{r}
# Combine SST data into one averaged raster 
sst_merged <- c(sst8, sst9, sst10, sst11, sst12)

sst_mean <- mean(sst_merged, na.rm = TRUE) 

# Convert average SST from Kelvin to Celsius
sst_c <- sst_mean - 273.15

# Check if coordinate reference systems, resolutions, and extents match
if(crs(depth) == crs(eez)) {
  print("Coordinate reference systems match")
} else{
  warning("Updating coordinate reference systems to match")
  crs(depth) <- crs(eez)
}

# check if coordinate reference systems match
if(crs(sst_c) == crs(eez)) {
  print("Coordinate reference systems match")
} else{
  warning("Updating coordinate reference systems to match")
  crs(sst_c) <- crs(eez)
}

# check if coordinate reference systems match
if(crs(sst_c) == crs(depth)) {
  print("Coordinate reference systems match")
} else{
  warning("Updating coordinate reference systems to match")
  crs(sst_c) <- crs(depth)
}

# Crop depth raster to match the extent of the SST raster
sst_ext <- ext(sst_c)
depth_crop <- crop(depth, sst_ext)

cat("=== Depth crop vs. SST resolution ===\n")
cat("Depth crop resolution:", res(depth_crop), "\n")
cat("Resolution:", res(sst_c), "\n")

# Resample the depth data to match the resolution of the SST data using the bilinear method approach
resample_depth <- resample(depth_crop, y = sst_c, method = "bilinear")

# Check that the depth and SST match in resolution, extent, and coordinate reference system

cat("=== Resampled depth vs. SST resolution ===\n")
cat("Resampled depth resolution:", res(resample_depth), "\n")
cat("SST resolution:", res(sst_c), "\n")

cat("=== Resampled depth vs. SST extent ===\n")
cat("Resampled depth extent:    "); print(ext(resample_depth))
cat("SST extent:    "); print(ext(sst_c))

cat("=== Resampled depth vs. SST crs ===\n")
cat("Resampled depth crs:", crs(resample_depth), "\n")
cat("SST crs:", crs(sst_c), "\n")

sst_depth <- c(sst_c, resample_depth)
```

Suitable range: 
Depth - 0-70 m 
Temp - 11-30 degress

```{r}
# Create depth matrix
rcl_depth <- matrix(c(
   -Inf, -70,  0,
   -70,  0,  1,
   0, Inf, 0
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Create SST matrix
rcl_SST <- matrix(c(
   -Inf, 11,  0,
   11,  30,  1,
   30, Inf, 0
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Reclassify depth
suitable_depth <- classify(resample_depth, rcl = rcl_depth)

# Reclassify temp
suitable_temp <- classify(sst_c, rcl = rcl_SST)

# Combine suitable zone rasters
suitable_zones <- c(suitable_depth, suitable_temp)

# Find suitable locations by multiplying suitable zones
suitable_locations <- lapp(suitable_zones, fun = function(sst, depth) sst * depth)
```

## Determine the most suitable EEZ

```{r}
# Set EEZ crs equal suitable_location crs 
sf::st_crs(eez) <- terra::crs(suitable_locations)

# Vectorize then rasterize  EEZ data
eez_raster <- rasterize(eez, suitable_locations, field = "rgn_id")

# Calculate the area of each cell
cell_sizes <- cellSize(suitable_locations, unit = "km", mask = TRUE)

# Make sure only cells classified as 1 contribute to area totals 
suitable_area <- mask(cell_sizes, suitable_locations, maskvalues = 0)

# Find the suitable area for each EEZ region
area_per_eez <- zonal(suitable_area, eez_raster, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
```

# Visualize

```{r}
area_per_eez |> 
  mutate(
    Region = c("Oregon", "Northern California", "Central California", "Southern California", "Washington") 
  ) |> 
  kable(
    col.names = c("Region ID", "Area $(km^2)$", "Region"),
    digits = 0
  ) |> 
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped")
```

From this table, we can determine that Central California has the most suitable oyster habitat when compared to the other four regions. By contrast, Northern California has the least suitable oyster habitat. 

```{r}
# Convert suitable area per eez to a dataframe for plotting
area_per_eez_df <- as_tibble(area_per_eez)

# Add EEZ polygons back in
map <- left_join(eez, area_per_eez_df, by = "rgn_id")

# Convert suitable area spatraster to polygons for plotting
area_poly <- as.polygons(suitable_area, dissolve = TRUE)

# Visualize
tm_shape(map) + 
  tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
  tm_polygons() +
  tm_fill(
    fill = "area", 
    col.scale = tm_scale(),
    fill_alpha = 0.8,
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Suitable habitat area by region (km²)", position = tm_pos_out("right"))
  ) +
  tm_text(text = "rgn", size = 0.3) + 
  tm_title(text = "Suitable Oyster Habitats of West Coast EEZs", size = 1) +
  tm_compass(position = c("left", "bottom"), size = 0.8) +
  tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_out("right", "bottom")) +
  tm_credits("Map 1", position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom")) + 
tm_shape(area_poly) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "#FFEA00") +
  tm_add_legend(
    type = "polygons", 
    labels = "Suitable Habitat Locations",
    fill = "#FFEA00",
    position = tm_pos_out("right")
  )
```

The yellow areas represent the suitable habitat locations for oysters, where sea surface temperature is between 11-30°C and depth is 0-70 meters below sea level. The map shoes that these areas are concentrated in the EEZs of Central California, Southern California, and Washington. 

Mediterranean mussel (*Mytilus galloprovincialis*) range:
125 - 200 m
10-20 deg C

# Making a generalizable function

arguments:
minimum and maximum sea surface temperature
minimum and maximum depth
species name
outputs:
map of EEZ regions colored by amount of suitable area
species name should be included in the map’s title
Remember, functions can be hard to debug! So it’s highly recommended that you build the workflow for a single species (not in a function). Then you can start translating your workflow into a function by identifying the pieces that need to be generalized.

Questions to ask yourself: which variables can stay the same for each species and which ones would need to change?
